generator.params.bud_break.note: A choice of the model's (leaf life, generator revision 44): a lateral bud needs vigour 2 (fabales' 1.3) to grow a long shoot. Once a leaf stayed one season, not two, more light reached the inner crown, more buds grew out, and the crown outgrew the module limit between 50 and 60 years; at 2 the open crowns peak at 0.65 to 0.77 million modules (0.87 million before) and keep their reference heights.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Neltuma velutina (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.7 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 2 records in 1 source); trunks 0.73, branches 0.67. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a spreading tree 6 to 9 m tall, often several-trunked and leaning, with dark, shaggy, furrowed bark, paired thorns, twice-divided leaves of many small velvety leaflets and yellow catkin spikes in spring; this proxy dies at 100 years and stands as a snag, losing its dead branches one by one. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.bud_years.note: Short shoots leaf out for up to 40 years while they have light, fitted with the seed plants' shoot spacing so that leaf area per crown area rises with age as the Urban Tree Database's city trees of Prosopis (P. chilensis, Glendale, Arizona) does, rather than falling once the crown has filled.

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card draws a cluster of its small leaves, a branchlet's worth, 0.26 m long, so that the crown keeps within the module limit; the seed plants' rules space the shoots from the card's area.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 4.5 m at 20 years and 8 m at 60; the 120-year keyframe is a snag. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark grey-brown bark, dull grey-green leaves, cream-yellow catkins. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): dark rough bark in shreddy furrowed strips; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Prosopis velutina, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.

traits.inflorescence.note: Jepson eFlora's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): inflorescence a spike-like raceme 5 to 15 cm long; the Fire Effects Information System gives cylindrical, pedunculate, spikelike racemes 5 to 7.6 cm long of hundreds of flowers.

appearance.organs.bloom.note: Its spike-like raceme drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c), as a spike, its pedicels too short to draw: 150 tiny pale yellow flowers about 4.5 mm long, by eye (the Fire Effects Information System says hundreds), on a raceme 8 cm long. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five small petals between five sepals, ten free stamens and one pistil, from the characters of Fabaceae and Neltuma by the rules at the flowering plants.

traits.division_order.note: Virginia Tech Dendrology's factsheet, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): leaves bipinnately compound, usually with only two major leaflets (pinnae), occasionally two or three pairs, each with 15 to 20 pairs of narrow, oblong minor leaflets. The University of Arizona Campus Arboretum gives two pinnae with 13 to 30 pairs of grey-green leaflets. The counts: pinnae 2 to 4, usually 2; leaflets on each pinna 26 to 60, typically 34 (17 pairs), the model's middle of the two sources; even-pinnate at both levels, as a mimosoid legume's leaf is.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: The leaf drawn as a twice-divided compound leaf (spec rework P4), its pinnae and their leaflets counted from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, a fern's frond stood in for it. By eye from photographs: the pinnae forking 30 degrees either side of the petiole's line, the leaflets standing out 75 degrees from theirs, a quarter as wide as long (Arizona sources give leaflets 4 to 13 mm long and about 2 mm wide).

traits.height_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, pp. 419-420), Prosopis juliflora var. velutina (P. velutina Wooton): genus usually armed with straight spines, leaves of 2 to 4 pinnae with many narrow leaflets, flowers small, greenish yellow, somewhat fragrant, in cylindric spikes, pods indehiscent, flattened but somewhat swollen; the species with pods much over 4 cm, leaflets commonly far more than 9 pairs; var. velutina with hairy foliage and leaflets under 15 mm; a large shrub or small tree along watercourses reaching 9 m or more with a trunk nearly 1 m across, a smaller shrub on grassland; April to August. The flora says 9 m 'or more'.

traits.spines.note: Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, pp. 475-478), genus Prosopis: trees or shrubs often armed with axillary spines or spiny stipules; leaves twice pinnate with 1 or 2 pairs of pinnae; flowers greenish, regular, in cylindric or globose axillary stalked spikes; petals 5; stamens 10, free, exserted; pod linear, leathery, not splitting, usually pulpy. He keeps velvet mesquite as P. chilensis subsp. velutina (p. 478): leaflets smaller than honey mesquite's (whose are 12-15 mm) and clearly hairy; armed with axillary spines (honey mesquite). The spines are axillary, so taken as shoot thorns; the genus as Abrams knew it also has spiny stipules in other species (screwbean), so this is the honey/velvet mesquite group's state, inferred from 'axillary'.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, pp. 419-420), Prosopis juliflora var. velutina (P. velutina Wooton): genus usually armed with straight spines, leaves of 2 to 4 pinnae with many narrow leaflets, flowers small, greenish yellow, somewhat fragrant, in cylindric spikes, pods indehiscent, flattened but somewhat swollen; the species with pods much over 4 cm, leaflets commonly far more than 9 pairs; var. velutina with hairy foliage and leaflets under 15 mm; a large shrub or small tree along watercourses reaching 9 m or more with a trunk nearly 1 m across, a smaller shrub on grassland; April to August.
